call_input.prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Create one finished, independent, flat graphic poster, portrait aspect ratio 2:3, full bleed. Not a photograph of a poster, no mockup, no panels. 요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력.

The single visual idea: a garden grows from the actual form of its Korean title. Typography is the principal organizing object, and the recognizable botanical growth obeys the terraces, edges, and open spaces created by the three real word groups.

Print exactly this complete Korean title ONCE and no other text:
밤에 피는 정원

Set the title in three rows, wrapping only at the two word spaces so that each two-syllable word remains intact. Use very large, heavy, clean, geometric Korean typography, not handwriting. The Hangul strokes and counters must be correct, complete, and immediately readable. Keep normal internal character spacing within each word. The first word begins near the left margin in the upper-middle; the second begins a little further right below it; the third returns toward the left below that. Maintain clear row separation. The resulting three immense word groups form an asymmetric stepped garden boundary, occupying the central height and most of the width. No letter is replaced with a plant, no foliage erases a stroke.

Use a near-black midnight-indigo unbroken background. The broad title strokes are matte warm moon-white, with sharply controlled edges. A restrained, precise botanical screen-print drawing grows directly from selected upward-facing stroke edges and the specific gaps in this title, never from an independent ground line. Choose one coherent climbing moonflower structure: thin muted yellow-green stems, simple heart-shaped leaves attached to continuous stems, a few recognizable pale lavender-white open trumpet flowers with five-pointed rims and a visible narrow base. Their roots visually meet the letter edges, and every stem travels predominantly upward toward the inter-row voids. Distribute growth unevenly according to each word's real shape: a taller branching stem rises from the broad upper ledge of the first word; lower stems nest between the second word's open spaces; one final stem follows the last word's outside edge. Leave broad portions of every letter bare. Flowers and leaves occupy the voids around and between letters, so that the letters determine the garden's outline. The title remains the first recognition; the plants are discovered along its borders on the second look.

Keep the graphic language planar and consistent: clean matte screen-print color shapes and delicate botanical line work with one common upper-left moonlight suggestion, no dimensional lettering, no shadows pretending that text is a physical object. Keep only slight localized ink variation, no blanket distressed texture. Calm dark peripheral negative space emphasizes this single living typographic object. Precise margins, no accidental tangencies, no symmetric floral border, no flowers filling every corner. No stars, moons, butterflies, additional objects, border frame, decorative glyphs, labels, subtitle, quotation marks, logos, watermark, numbering, style names, or microtext.
